query: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi has high saturation magnetization but a low coercive field, and reported single-phase fcc high-entropy alloys derived from it have coercive fields no greater than 100 Oe in the reported magnetic measurements. What single intervention could overcome this coercivity limitation? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted change relative to single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a matched derivative, the relevant compositional, structural, and measurement boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a controlled density of coherent B2-ordered (Fe,Co)Al nanoprecipitates inside an otherwise single-phase fcc FeCoNi matrix will raise the room-temperature coercive field (Hc) by at least a factor of three (≥ 300 Oe) while reducing the saturation magnetization (Ms) by no more than 10 % relative to solution-treated single-phase fcc FeCoNi of matched grain size.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic FeCoNi polycrystalline bulk alloy, single-phase fcc (Fm-3m), average grain size ≈50 µm, solution-treated 1000 °C/1 h and water-quenched; typical Ms ≈1.4 T and Hc ≤ 100 Oe at 300 K.
generation.intervention: Add 8 at.% Al to give Fe29Co29Ni29Al13 (atomic %), solution-treat 1000 °C/1 h, water-quench, then age at 600 °C for 4 h to precipitate coherent B2-ordered (Fe,Co)Al nanoparticles (target radius 3–10 nm, volume fraction 5–10 %).
generation.conditions: Bulk samples; aging in Ar atmosphere; magnetic properties measured at 300 K by vibrating-sample magnetometry (maximum field ±20 kOe); identical grain size preserved by final light recrystallisation if required.
generation.structural_mediator: Nanometer-scale coherent B2 precipitates embedded in the fcc matrix, generating local strain fields and chemical ordering while maintaining overall fcc crystallography.
generation.mechanism: 1) Domain-wall pinning at the elastic and chemical potential wells surrounding the coherent (Fe,Co)Al precipitates; 2) locally enhanced magnetocrystalline anisotropy arising from B2 chemical ordering and associated tetragonal distortion. The combined pinning and anisotropy impede domain-wall motion, raising Hc without strongly suppressing exchange or Ms.
generation.predicted_outcome: Room-temperature coercive field Hc ≥ 300 Oe (≥3× the ≤100 Oe baseline) with Ms ≥ 1.25 T (≤10 % drop) and remanence Mr ≥ 0.7 T. The aged alloy therefore overcomes the typical coercivity ceiling of single-phase fcc FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloys.
generation.baseline: Solution-treated FeCoNi or FeCoNiAl0.13 without aging: single-phase fcc with no resolvable B2 ordering, Hc ≤ 100 Oe, Ms ≈1.4 T.
generation.boundary: Al additions 5–15 at.% and aging temperatures 550–650 °C that retain a majority fcc matrix and keep B2 precipitate size below ~20 nm; grain size ≥10 µm to avoid grain-size–controlled coercivity; measurements at 300 K in bulk (not thin-film) form.
generation.uncertainty: Magnitude of anisotropy contribution from B2 order may be insufficient if precipitates over-coarsen or if Al segregates to grain boundaries, potentially limiting Hc increase; Ms reduction could exceed 10 % if B2 fraction is too high. No direct data yet confirm the quantitative effect in FeCoNiAl.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of Fe29Co29Ni29Al13 samples: (A) solution-treated only; (B) solution-treated then aged 600 °C/4 h. Confirm identical average grain size by EBSD. Characterise precipitates in B by TEM and synchrotron XRD. Measure full hysteresis loops (±20 kOe) at 300 K for both sets.
measurements: Volume fraction and ordering parameter of B2 phase (XRD)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the aged sample (B) shows Hc ≤ 2 × Hc of the unaged control (A) or absolute Hc ≤ 100 Oe, the hypothesis is falsified; alternatively, if Ms in (B) falls more than 10 % below (A), the hypothesis is also considered falsified.
